title: Alma begins explaining restoration
summary: Alma tells his son he will explain restoration, noting that some have distorted scripture and that his son has been troubled about the subject.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says some have wrested the scriptures and gone far astray concerning restoration.
Alma perceives that his son's mind has been worried about restoration and says he will explain it.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, age, posture, and appearance of both people are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: But behold, I will explain it unto thee.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is reported teaching, not a narrated supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a visual personification of restoration or scripture being physically distorted.

title: Restoration and the body
summary: Alma explains that restoration accords with God's justice: the soul is restored to the body, and people are judged according to their works and heart's desires.

explicit_facts.text: Alma teaches that all things are to be restored to their proper order and that the soul is restored to its body, with every part of the body restored to itself.
Alma teaches that people are judged according to their works and that good works and desires lead to restoration to good at the last day.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues speaking to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: No resurrection or judgment scene is narrated as currently occurring; the setting and characters' appearance are not specified.

narration.text: all things should be restored to their proper order
men should be judged according to their works

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Restoration and judgment are teachings in Alma's speech, not present-tense visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict resurrected people, bodies being reassembled, or a judgment scene as happening now.

title: Restored according to desires
summary: Alma teaches that evil works and desires bring an evil restoration, while good desires bring happiness and good; he describes contrasting outcomes.

explicit_facts.text: Alma teaches that the wicked are restored to evil and describes mortality raised to immortality and corruption to incorruption, with contrasting outcomes.
Alma teaches that each person is restored according to desires of good or evil and receives an evil reward for desiring evil.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks continuously to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: No afterlife destination, kingdom, or personified outcome is visibly described in the present scene.

narration.text: all things shall be restored to their proper order
The one raised to happiness according to his desires of happiness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The contrast of one outcome on one hand and the other on the other is figurative teaching, not a narrated tableau.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict heaven, hell, or a supernatural division of people as a present event.

title: Repentance and redemption
summary: Alma teaches that one who repents and desires righteousness to the end is rewarded with righteousness, and describes the redeemed as delivered from endless night.

explicit_facts.text: Alma teaches that one who repents and desires righteousness until the end of life is rewarded unto righteousness.
Alma describes the redeemed of the Lord as delivered from endless night and says they are their own judges, whether to do good or evil.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues his teaching to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: The redeemed are described in doctrine, not shown as a separate visible group.

narration.text: If he hath repented of his sins

doctrinal_or_story_notes: "Endless night of darkness" is figurative teaching; do not render it as a literal place or event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show people emerging from a literal night or depict the redeemed in a supernatural scene.

title: The way is prepared
summary: Alma teaches that God's decrees are unalterable and the way is prepared for anyone willing to walk in it and be saved; he warns his son against further offense.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says God's decrees are unalterable and a way is prepared for whoever will walk therein and be saved.
Alma tells his son not to risk another offense against God on points of doctrine where he has risked committing sin.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the son's response are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: do not risk one more offense against your God
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prepared way is a teaching, not a described road or visible supernatural construction.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal road, divine appearance, or a new act of sin.

title: Wickedness is not happiness
summary: Alma rejects the idea that a person can be restored from sin to happiness. He teaches that a carnal state is contrary to God's nature and happiness.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says wickedness never was happiness and that restoration does not restore a person from sin to happiness.
Alma describes those in a natural or carnal state as in bitterness and iniquity, without God in the world, and contrary to happiness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues speaking to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: The metaphorical conditions are not described as physical appearances.

narration.text: they are without God in the world

doctrinal_or_story_notes: "Gall of bitterness" and "bonds of iniquity" are figures of speech in the teaching.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal bitterness, bonds, or a supernatural state.

title: The meaning of restoration
summary: Alma asks whether restoration places something in a state opposite to its nature, then explains that it brings back like for like: evil for evil and good for good.

explicit_facts.text: Alma asks whether restoration takes something from a natural state and places it in an unnatural state or opposite state.
Alma says restoration brings back evil for evil and good, righteousness, justice, or mercy for their like.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues his explanation to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: No objects or people representing the abstract categories are specified.

narration.text: the meaning of the word restoration is to bring back again
good for that which is good

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The paired qualities are explanatory teaching, not separate visual events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not personify good, evil, justice, or mercy.

title: Do good continually
summary: Alma urges his son to be merciful, just, righteous, and continually good, teaching that such acts return to the doer and that restoration condemns the sinner rather than justifying him.

explicit_facts.text: Alma urges his son to be merciful to his brethren, deal justly, judge righteously, and do good continually, promising corresponding rewards.
Alma says what a person sends out returns and is restored, and that restoration condemns the sinner and does not justify him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma concludes his teaching to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: The brethren are mentioned but not shown or described as present.

narration.text: For that which ye do send out shall return unto you again

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The return of deeds is a teaching, not a narrated physical action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a deed returning as a literal object or add a response from Alma's son.
